37 In the circuit shown, a battery of negligible internal resistance is connected in series with a pair of
fixed resistors R1 and R2.
60 Ω
R1
6.0 V
X
R2
20 Ω
Y
The circuit is to be used to test whether the electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a particular cell is 1.5 V.
The cell is connected between terminals X and Y in parallel with R2 and in series with a
galvanometer.
Which statement about the test is correct?
A
Any non-zero reading on the galvanometer means the cell has an e.m.f. of 1.5 V.
B
The battery does not need to have an e.m.f. of 6.0 V.
C
The cell may be connected either way round between X and Y.
D
The galvanometer does not need a scale calibrated in amperes.

hints: Notice $R_1 = 60\,\Omega$ and $R_2 = 20\,\Omega$ form a potential divider across the $6.0\text{ V}$ battery, so calculate the p.d. across $R_2$ between X and Y.
Think of the cell plus galvanometer loop across $R_2$ as a balance: current is zero only when the cell e.m.f. exactly equals and opposes the $R_2$ p.d.
Ask yourself whether the test needs the size of any unbalanced current, or only whether the galvanometer current is zero or non-zero.
walkthrough: Calculate the divider voltage across $R_2$. Total resistance is $60 + 20 = 80\,\Omega$, so current is $I = 6.0/80 = 0.075\text{ A}$ and $V_{XY} = I R_2 = 0.075 \times 20 = 1.5\text{ V}$.
The test cell is connected across X-Y with the galvanometer in series. This forms a second loop where the $1.5\text{ V}$ divider p.d. and the cell e.m.f. act against each other.
If the cell is connected with the correct polarity and its e.m.f. is exactly $1.5\text{ V}$, the net e.m.f. in that loop is zero, so galvanometer current is zero. This is the null condition.
Any e.m.f. different from $1.5\text{ V}$, wrong polarity, or different supply voltage destroys the $1.5\text{ V}$ balance and gives a non-zero deflection.
Therefore the galvanometer acts only as a zero detector. Its scale does not need to read amperes. This is option D.

A.explanation: A non-zero galvanometer current means the p.d. across $R_2$ and the cell e.m.f. are unbalanced, so the cell is not $1.5\text{ V}$. Zero reading is the test for $1.5\text{ V}$.

B.explanation: With fixed $60\,\Omega$ and $20\,\Omega$ resistors, only a $6.0\text{ V}$ supply gives $1.5\text{ V}$ across $R_2$ from $V = 6.0 \times 20/(60+20)$.

C.explanation: The cell must oppose the p.d. across $R_2$ so the two voltages can cancel. Reversed polarity would drive a large current and can never give a null.

D.explanation: This is a null method, so the galvanometer is only used to detect zero current, not to measure the value of the current in amperes.
